=== get_data.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# MathScholar (team 1) — fetch and render the corpus.
#
#   Abramowitz & Stegun, "Handbook of Mathematical Functions", NBS AMS-55 (1964)
#   Internet Archive item: handbookofmathem1964abra
#
# What this does, in order:
#   1. downloads the source PDF into  data/raw/   (skipped if already there)
#   2. renders every PDF page to      data/pages/ as 300-dpi GRAYSCALE PNG
#   3. spot-checks the printed<->PDF page offset against the PDF's text layer
#   4. prints the counts that data/provenance.md records
#
# Both output directories are gitignored — the corpus is ~1 GB and is never
# committed. This script is what recreates it on a clean machine.
#
# Idempotent and resumable: a page whose PNG already exists is skipped, so an
# interrupted run is fixed by re-running it.
#
# Usage:
#   bash scripts/get_data.sh                 # full corpus (~1082 pages)
#   LIMIT=20 bash scripts/get_data.sh        # first 20 pages only (quick check)
#   RENDER_DPI=150 bash scripts/get_data.sh  # lower-res pass
#   FORCE=1 bash scripts/get_data.sh         # re-render pages that already exist
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

# --- what we are fetching -----------------------------------------------------
ARCHIVE_ID="handbookofmathem1964abra"
PDF_URL="https://archive.org/download/${ARCHIVE_ID}/${ARCHIVE_ID}.pdf"
RAW_DIR="data/raw"
PAGES_DIR="data/pages"
PDF_PATH="${RAW_DIR}/${ARCHIVE_ID}.pdf"

# Recorded at first download (2026-08-08). Re-runs verify against it so a
# truncated or silently-changed download cannot poison the corpus.
EXPECTED_SHA256="2e0205d8a35a0f544b7cd4f16fde91ba38f1527febedb37fbdc9b85a6e7b214a"

# --- render settings (config.yaml: ocr.render_dpi = 300) ----------------------
RENDER_DPI="${RENDER_DPI:-300}"

# Printed page N is PDF page N+32 — the book has 32 front-matter pages (cover,
# title, preface, contents) that carry no printed arabic folio.
FRONT_MATTER_OFFSET="${FRONT_MATTER_OFFSET:-32}"

LIMIT="${LIMIT:-0}"     # 0 = all pages
FORCE="${FORCE:-0}"     # 1 = re-render pages that already exist

echo "=============================================================="
echo " MathScholar corpus — Abramowitz & Stegun 1964 (NBS AMS-55)"
echo " public domain: work of the U.S. Government, 17 U.S.C. Sec.105"
echo "=============================================================="

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Pick an interpreter that can import PyMuPDF.
#    We render with PyMuPDF rather than `pdftoppm` because poppler is not
#    installed by default on Windows, and pymupdf is already a pinned
#    dependency — so this script runs on all three of our machines unchanged.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (an array, so a venv path containing spaces and the multi-word `uv run python`
#  fallback both survive quoting)
PY_CMD=()
for cand in "$REPO_ROOT/.venv/Scripts/python.exe" "$REPO_ROOT/.venv/bin/python" python3 python; do
  if "$cand" -c "import pymupdf" >/dev/null 2>&1; then PY_CMD=("$cand"); break; fi
done
if [ ${#PY_CMD[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  if uv run python -c "import pymupdf" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    PY_CMD=(uv run python)
  else
    echo "ERROR: PyMuPDF not available. Run:  uv sync --extra dev" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi
echo "[env] renderer: $("${PY_CMD[@]}" -c 'import pymupdf,sys; print("PyMuPDF", pymupdf.__doc__.split()[1], "on Python", sys.version.split()[0])')"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Download the PDF (78.6 MB). Resumable; skipped when already present.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
mkdir -p "$RAW_DIR" "$PAGES_DIR"

if [ -s "$PDF_PATH" ]; then
  echo "[1/4] source PDF already present — skipping download ($PDF_PATH)"
else
  echo "[1/4] downloading $PDF_URL"
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl -L --fail --retry 3 -C - -o "$PDF_PATH" "$PDF_URL"
  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    wget -c -O "$PDF_PATH" "$PDF_URL"
  else
    echo "ERROR: need curl or wget to download the corpus." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# Integrity check — a half-finished download is the classic silent corpus bug.
ACTUAL_SHA256="$("${PY_CMD[@]}" -c "
import hashlib,sys
h=hashlib.sha256()
with open(sys.argv[1],'rb') as f:
    for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1<<20), b''): h.update(b)
print(h.hexdigest())
" "$PDF_PATH")"
echo "[1/4] sha256: $ACTUAL_SHA256"
if [ -n "$EXPECTED_SHA256" ] && [ "$ACTUAL_SHA256" != "$EXPECTED_SHA256" ]; then
  echo "WARNING: sha256 differs from the recorded value in this script." >&2
  echo "         recorded: $EXPECTED_SHA256" >&2
  echo "         got:      $ACTUAL_SHA256" >&2
  echo "         Delete $PDF_PATH and re-run if the download was interrupted." >&2
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2-4. Render, spot-check the page offset, and report counts.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
RENDER_DPI="$RENDER_DPI" \
FRONT_MATTER_OFFSET="$FRONT_MATTER_OFFSET" \
PDF_PATH="$PDF_PATH" \
PAGES_DIR="$PAGES_DIR" \
LIMIT="$LIMIT" \
FORCE="$FORCE" \
"${PY_CMD[@]}" - <<'PY'
import os
import re
import sys
import time

import pymupdf

pdf_path = os.environ["PDF_PATH"]
pages_dir = os.environ["PAGES_DIR"]
dpi = int(os.environ["RENDER_DPI"])
offset = int(os.environ["FRONT_MATTER_OFFSET"])
limit = int(os.environ["LIMIT"])
force = os.environ["FORCE"] == "1"


def page_stem(pdf_index_1based: int) -> str:
    """Filename stem for a PDF page.

    The number in the stem is the PRINTED page number, because that is what we
    cite and what every page list in summary.md is written in (see
    summary.md 3f: `as_p0255` -> printed page 255).

    Front-matter pages have no printed arabic folio, so they get an `as_f`
    stem keyed by PDF index instead. `ingest/loader.py` drops them.
    """
    printed = pdf_index_1based - offset
    if printed >= 1:
        return f"as_p{printed:04d}"
    return f"as_f{pdf_index_1based:04d}"


doc = pymupdf.open(pdf_path)
n_pdf_pages = doc.page_count
last = n_pdf_pages if limit <= 0 else min(limit, n_pdf_pages)

print(f"[2/4] rendering {last} of {n_pdf_pages} PDF pages "
      f"@ {dpi} dpi grayscale -> {pages_dir}/")
print(f"      naming: printed page N -> as_pNNNN.png   (printed N = PDF N+{offset})")

rendered = skipped = 0
t0 = time.time()
for i in range(last):
    out = os.path.join(pages_dir, page_stem(i + 1) + ".png")
    if os.path.exists(out) and not force:
        skipped += 1
        continue
    # csGRAY: the scan is monochrome typeset; grayscale keeps thin sub/superscript
    # strokes that hard binarisation would thicken, at 1/3 the disk of RGB.
    pix = doc.load_page(i).get_pixmap(dpi=dpi, colorspace=pymupdf.csGRAY)
    pix.save(out)
    rendered += 1
    if rendered % 50 == 0:
        done = rendered + skipped
        rate = rendered / max(time.time() - t0, 1e-9)
        print(f"      {done}/{last} pages ({rate:.1f} pages/s)", flush=True)

print(f"[2/4] done: {rendered} rendered, {skipped} already present")

# --- 3. spot-check the printed <-> PDF offset --------------------------------
# Read the printed folio out of the PDF's own text layer on a few sample pages
# and confirm it equals (pdf_index - offset). This is the check that stops a
# whole downstream sprint from citing pages 32 off.
print(f"[3/4] verifying the page offset (expect printed N = PDF N+{offset})")


def folio_found(text: str, expected: int) -> bool:
    """True if `expected` appears as a running folio on this page.

    The folio sits at the very start or very end of the page's text, either
    alone ("260") or fused to the running head ("1028  LAPLACE TRANSFORMS").
    Anchoring to the line edge is what keeps this from matching the equation
    numbers and table cells that fill these pages.
    """
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    for ln in lines[:3] + lines[-3:]:
        if re.match(rf"^\W*{expected}\b", ln) or re.search(rf"\b{expected}\W*$", ln):
            return True
    return False


samples = [s for s in (255, 287, 292, 300, 632, 1060) if s <= n_pdf_pages]
confirmed = sum(folio_found(doc.load_page(p - 1).get_text(), p - offset) for p in samples)
# Control: the same test with a deliberately wrong offset must NOT pass, or the
# check is matching noise rather than folios.
control = sum(folio_found(doc.load_page(p - 1).get_text(), p) for p in samples)
for p in samples:
    hit = folio_found(doc.load_page(p - 1).get_text(), p - offset)
    print(f"      PDF p.{p:>4} -> printed {p - offset:>4}  {'OK' if hit else '-- (no folio in text layer)'}")
print(f"      confirmed {confirmed}/{len(samples)}; control at wrong offset {control}/{len(samples)}")

if confirmed == 0 or control >= confirmed:
    print(f"      WARNING: could not confirm printed N = PDF N+{offset} from the text layer.")
    print("      Open data/pages/as_p0255.png — it must be the Gamma-function page 255.")

# --- 4. report the numbers that go into data/provenance.md -------------------
pngs = sorted(f for f in os.listdir(pages_dir) if f.endswith(".png"))
content = [f for f in pngs if f.startswith("as_p")]
front = [f for f in pngs if f.startswith("as_f")]
bytes_pdf = os.path.getsize(pdf_path)
bytes_png = sum(os.path.getsize(os.path.join(pages_dir, f)) for f in pngs)

# Reference word count from the ARCHIVE's own OCR text layer. This is NOT the
# number validate() asserts: the >=60,000-word floor must come from OUR OCR
# (summary.md 10). It is recorded only to show the corpus is large enough.
words = sum(len(doc.load_page(i).get_text().split()) for i in range(n_pdf_pages))

print("[4/4] corpus summary  (these are the numbers in data/provenance.md)")
print(f"      PDF pages            : {n_pdf_pages}")
print(f"      page images rendered : {len(pngs)}  ({len(content)} printed + {len(front)} front matter)")
print(f"      printed page range   : 1 .. {n_pdf_pages - offset}")
print(f"      source PDF size      : {bytes_pdf / 1e6:.1f} MB")
print(f"      page images size     : {bytes_png / 1e9:.2f} GB")
print(f"      words (archive OCR)  : {words}   <- reference only, not the graded count")
print(f"      render dpi / mode    : {dpi} / grayscale")
doc.close()

if limit <= 0 and len(pngs) != n_pdf_pages:
    print(f"ERROR: expected {n_pdf_pages} page images, found {len(pngs)}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)
PY

echo
echo "Corpus ready. Nothing here is committed:"
echo "  $RAW_DIR/    source PDF      (gitignored)"
echo "  $PAGES_DIR/  page images     (gitignored)"
echo "Next: scripts/build_index.sh turns these into the vector index."
get_data.sh is well-built for this — idempotent, resumable, LIMIT env var, sha256 + page-offset verification. Now the Kaggle tooling.

"""Build KAGGLE/kaggle.ipynb (MathScholar Step 16) from a percent-format source.

Percent format keeps the notebook authorable as plain text:
    # %% [markdown]   -> markdown cell ('# ' prefix stripped from each line)
    # %%              -> code cell
"""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SRC = r'''
# %% [markdown]
# # MathScholar · Step 16 — Baseline Full-Book OCR on Kaggle GPU
#
# **Project:** MathScholar (team 1) — agentic RAG over *Abramowitz & Stegun,
# Handbook of Mathematical Functions*, NBS AMS-55 (1964).
# **Step owner:** S1 · Anuron Maitro (2105037) · branch `Anuron-step-16`
# **Plan reference:** `plan.md` §8 Step 16 and §11 (Kaggle walkthrough).
#
# ---
#
# ## What this notebook is for
#
# Every stage of our knowledge-base pipeline is now implemented and merged
# (Steps 1–15). This notebook is the first time the **vision half of the pipeline
# runs at full corpus scale**, and it produces the single most important number
# in A2 form §5: the **"BEFORE" baseline** that Sprint 4's fine-tune has to beat.
#
# It runs, in order:
#
# | Stage | Module | Owner | What it does here |
# |---|---|---|---|
# | 1 Ingest | `ingest/loader.py` | S2 | `data/pages/*.png` -> `list[Page]`, `doc_id` = chapter |
# | 1 Clean | `ingest/preprocess.py` | S3 | deskew · light denoise · CLAHE (grayscale, no binarisation) |
# | 2 Layout | `vision/layout.py` | S1 | two-column split -> blocks -> `list[Region]` in reading order |
# | 3 OCR | `vision/ocr.py` | S2 | **pretrained** `facebook/nougat-base` -> `.mmd` per page + `list[Chunk]` |
# | 9 Metrics | `eval/metrics.py` | S3 | char-level F1 + exact-formula-match vs the 3 gold pages |
#
# Note the OCR reader here is the **pretrained baseline, not fine-tuned**
# (`plan.md` Step 11 point 6). Fine-tuning is Sprint 4 / Step 28. That is the
# entire point: this run is the control we measure improvement against.
#
# ## What it deliberately does NOT do
#
# - **No embedding / no index build.** Steps 14–15 (`embed.py`, `store.py`) sit
#   *downstream* of OCR and are not exercised here; the full chain is rebuilt in
#   Step 30 once the fine-tuned reader exists. Running BGE-M3 over the whole
#   corpus now would burn GPU hours on an index we are going to throw away.
# - **No hook seams.** We call the pipeline stages directly rather than
#   `pipeline.build_knowledge_base()`, so the `AFTER_OCR` seam (where
#   `governance/pii.py` scrubs text) does not fire. That is correct for this step:
#   we are producing raw reader output for later inspection and annotation, and
#   PII scrubbing belongs to the indexing path that Step 30 runs.
#
# ## Deliverables this notebook produces (all inside one downloadable zip)
#
# 1. `data/ocr/*.mmd` — one raw Nougat transcript per page (~1040 files)
# 2. `data/ocr/meta.jsonl` — per-chunk `ocr_confidence` + `bbox` sidecar
# 3. `data/ocr/failures.json` — **the honest degenerate-page list** (form §5)
# 4. `step16_reports/baseline_metrics.{json,md}` — the BEFORE numbers
# 5. `step16_reports/ocr_coverage.csv` — per-page character/word coverage
# 6. `step16_reports/run_manifest.json` — full reproducibility record

# %% [markdown]
# ## ⚠️ Read this before you run: the two-phase protocol
#
# This notebook has a single switch, `RUN_MODE`, and you are expected to run it
# **twice** — smoke first, then full.
#
# ```
# RUN_MODE = "smoke"   ->  20 hand-picked pages, ~15 min   <- DO THIS FIRST
# RUN_MODE = "full"    ->  all ~1040 pages,      ~2-3 h
# ```
#
# **Why the smoke run is not optional.** Neither `layout.detect` nor
# `ocr.transcribe` has ever been run at corpus scale by anyone on the team —
# Step 10's acceptance bar was *one* page (printed 360) and Step 11's was
# "20 pages produce sane LaTeX", which was never actually executed because the
# 1.4 GB Nougat download was not on any of our machines.
#
# The asymmetry is stark, and it is the whole argument:
#
# - smoke run that fails  -> you lose ~15 minutes and learn exactly what broke
# - full run that fails at page 800, or silently writes 1040 files of garbage
#   -> you lose 2–3 hours out of Kaggle's ~30 GPU-hr weekly budget, **and** you
#   still have to debug it afterwards
#
# The 20 smoke pages are chosen to span chapters and page *types* — dense numeric
# tables (where Nougat's repetition-degeneration failure mode actually bites),
# two-column formula pages, and prose — and they **include all three gold pages**
# (printed 243, 255, 360), so the smoke run already previews the real BEFORE
# numbers before you commit to the long job.
#
# **Belt and braces:** even in `"full"` mode this notebook OCRs the smoke subset
# *first* and runs an automatic sanity gate on it before touching the rest of the
# book. That costs nothing — `ocr.transcribe` skips any page whose `.mmd` already
# exists — so the gated pages are simply done early rather than twice.

# %% [markdown]
# ## Kaggle session settings this notebook expects
#
# Set by `kernel-metadata.json`, so `kaggle kernels push` configures them for you:
#
# | Setting | Value | Why |
# |---|---|---|
# | Accelerator | **GPU T4 x2** (`NvidiaTeslaT4`) | `configs/config.yaml` sets `device: cuda`; Nougat on CPU is an overnight run |
# | Internet | **On** | clones the repo, downloads the A&S PDF and the model weights |
# | Persistence | `/kaggle/working` | the only directory that survives into the notebook output |
#
# **Session limits (`plan.md` §11.4).** A session dies at ~9 h interactive / ~12 h
# committed, and after ~20 min idle. Push with *Save & Run All* semantics (which
# is what `kaggle kernels push` does) so the job survives your laptop closing.
# If it does time out, see the **resume** cell below — the OCR loop is resumable
# and you restart from where it stopped rather than from zero.

# %%
# ============================================================================
# CONFIGURATION — the only cell you normally edit.
# ============================================================================

# "smoke" = 20 pages (~15 min, includes all 3 gold pages)  <- run this FIRST
# "full"  = every content page (~1040, ~2-3 h)
RUN_MODE = "smoke"

# Our repo is public, which is what makes this one-line clone possible.
# Step 16 changes no source file, so we clone `main` (Steps 1-15 merged);
# the notebook itself lives outside the repo, in KAGGLE/.
REPO_URL = "https://github.com/anuronmaitro/doc-agent-1.git"
REPO_BRANCH = "main"

WORK_DIR = "/kaggle/working"
REPO_DIR = WORK_DIR + "/repo"
STAGE_DIR = WORK_DIR + "/step16_out"
ZIP_PATH = WORK_DIR + "/mathscholar_step16_baseline_ocr.zip"

# The three A1 gold pages, hand-transcribed in grading_kit/labels.jsonl.
# These are TEST-split pages (summary.md 4h) and give the BEFORE number.
GOLD_PRINTED_PAGES = [243, 255, 360]

# 20 smoke pages spanning chapters AND page types. Dense-table pages are in here
# on purpose: that is Nougat's known repetition-degeneration failure mode, so a
# smoke run without tables would be a smoke run that cannot fail informatively.
SMOKE_PRINTED_PAGES = [
    1, 65, 100, 227, 243, 255, 295, 331, 360, 435,
    503, 587, 685, 721, 803, 875, 925, 1011, 1019, 1028,

# requirements.lock pins transformers==4.44.2; we install the same version on

TRANSFORMERS_PIN = "4.44.2"

assert RUN_MODE in ("smoke", "full"), "RUN_MODE must be 'smoke' or 'full'"
print("RUN_MODE           :", RUN_MODE)

print("gold pages         :", GOLD_PRINTED_PAGES)

# %% [markdown]

# %% [markdown]
# ### Dependencies
#
# We deliberately do **not** `pip install -r requirements.lock` here. That lock
# pins `torch==2.3.1`, which would fight Kaggle's preinstalled CUDA build of
# torch, take ten-plus minutes, and could leave us on a CPU wheel without
# noticing. Kaggle's image already ships torch/CUDA, numpy, OpenCV, Pillow,
# pydantic and PyYAML.
#
# So we install only the two things that actually differ:
#
# - **`pymupdf`** — `scripts/get_data.sh` renders the PDF with it, and it is not
#   in Kaggle's base image.
# - **`transformers==4.44.2`** — pinned to match `requirements.lock` exactly, so
#   the Nougat generation path here is byte-for-byte the one our lockfile
#   describes. (This must happen *before* the first `import transformers`, which
#   is why no earlier cell imports it.)

# %%
subprocess.run(

# %% [markdown]
# ## 2 · Get the corpus
#
# `scripts/get_data.sh` (Step 3, S3) is the reproducible corpus path — the same
# script a grader runs on a clean machine. It downloads the A&S PDF, verifies its
# **sha256** against a recorded value (a truncated download is the classic silent
# corpus bug), renders every page to 300-dpi grayscale PNG, and then *spot-checks
# the printed-to-PDF page offset against the PDF's own text layer* — the check
# that stops a whole sprint from citing pages 32 off.
#
# We render the **whole book even in smoke mode**, on purpose:
#
# - it is only ~4-5 minutes, and
# - `LIMIT=20` would render the first 20 *PDF* pages, which are all front matter
#   (`as_f*`) — and `ingest/loader.py` drops those, so a limited render would
#   hand us **zero content pages**. Rendering everything and then subsetting the
#   `Page` list is both simpler and correct.
#
# It is idempotent: pages already present are skipped.

# %%
t0 = time.time()
subprocess.run(["bash", "scripts/get_data.sh"], check=True)
T_RENDER = time.time() - t0
print("\n[timing] corpus fetch + render: %.1f min" % (T_RENDER / 60))

# %% [markdown]
# ## 3 · Resume support (only matters if a previous run timed out)
#
# `ocr.transcribe` skips any page whose `.mmd` already exists, so a re-run
# continues instead of restarting. `/kaggle/working` does **not** persist across
# notebook versions, though — so to actually resume you must feed the previous
# run's output back in:
#
# 1. previous run finished/timed out -> its `/kaggle/working` became that
#    version's **Output**
# 2. in this notebook: **Add Input -> Notebook Output -> (previous version)**
# 3. re-run — the cell below copies any `.mmd` it finds under `/kaggle/input`
#    into `data/ocr/`, and OCR picks up from there
#
# On a first run this reports `0 seeded`, which is expected.

# %%
import glob

os.makedirs("data/ocr", exist_ok=True)
seeded = 0
for src in glob.glob("/kaggle/input/**/*.mmd", recursive=True):
    dst = os.path.join("data/ocr", os.path.basename(src))
    if not os.path.exists(dst):
        shutil.copy2(src, dst)
        seeded += 1
for name in ("meta.jsonl", "failures.json"):
    for src in glob.glob("/kaggle/input/**/" + name, recursive=True):
        dst = os.path.join("data/ocr", name)
        if not os.path.exists(dst):
            shutil.copy2(src, dst)

print("seeded %d cached .mmd transcripts from /kaggle/input" % seeded)
print("data/ocr now holds %d .mmd files" % len(glob.glob("data/ocr/*.mmd")))

# %% [markdown]
# ## 4 · Ingest -> clean -> layout
#
# Three stages, all CPU-bound except the optional table-transformer pass:
#
# - **`loader.load_pages`** globs `data/pages/as_p*.png`, drops front matter and
#   blank versos (measured ink-variance threshold), and sets `Page.doc_id` to the
#   **chapter id** — `doc_id` *is* the chapter for us (`summary.md` §3f), which is
#   what makes the train/val/test split leak-proof by construction.
# - **`preprocess.run`** deskews only pages measurably crooked (a dead zone
#   avoids resampling ~94% of pages for nothing), lightly denoises with a
#   bilateral filter, and applies CLAHE. Output stays **grayscale** — hard
#   binarisation thickens the thin sub/superscript strokes this corpus is made of.
# - **`layout.detect`** finds the two-column gutter, segments blocks within each
#   column, classifies them (text/table/figure/heading), and emits regions in
#   **reading order** — left column fully, then right. Reading order is not
#   cosmetic: our char-F1 uses a longest-common-*subsequence*, so scrambled
#   regions score ~0.42 where a bag-of-characters metric would wrongly say 1.00.
#
# **Smoke mode subsets the page list here**, before preprocess and layout — not
# via `ocr.transcribe`'s `limit_pages` guard. Both give 20 pages of OCR, but
# subsetting early also skips ~1020 pages of preprocessing and layout, turning a
# ~25-minute smoke run into a ~2-minute one.

# %%
from doc_agent import config
from doc_agent.eval import metrics
from doc_agent.ingest import loader, preprocess
from doc_agent.vision import layout
from doc_agent.vision import ocr as ocr_mod

cfg = config.load()
print("config device:", cfg["device"], "| ocr model:", cfg["ocr"]["model"])
print("layout model :", cfg["layout"]["model"])

t0 = time.time()
all_pages = loader.load_pages(cfg)
T_LOAD = time.time() - t0
print("\n[loader] %d content pages (front matter + blank versos dropped) in %.1fs"
      % (len(all_pages), T_LOAD))

smoke_ids = {"as_p%04d" % p for p in SMOKE_PRINTED_PAGES}
gold_ids = {"as_p%04d" % p for p in GOLD_PRINTED_PAGES}

if RUN_MODE == "smoke":
    pages = [p for p in all_pages if p.id in smoke_ids]
    missing = smoke_ids - {p.id for p in pages}
    assert not missing, "smoke pages missing from the corpus: %s" % sorted(missing)
    print("[smoke] subset to %d pages" % len(pages))
else:
    pages = all_pages
    print("[full] processing all %d pages" % len(pages))

t0 = time.time()
pages = preprocess.run(pages, cfg)
T_PREPROCESS = time.time() - t0
print("[preprocess] %d pages in %.1f min" % (len(pages), T_PREPROCESS / 60))

t0 = time.time()
regions = layout.detect(pages, cfg)
T_LAYOUT = time.time() - t0
kinds = {}
for r in regions:
    kinds[r.kind] = kinds.get(r.kind, 0) + 1
print("[layout] %d regions from %d pages in %.1f min" % (len(regions), len(pages), T_LAYOUT / 60))
print("[layout] region kinds:", dict(sorted(kinds.items())))
print("[layout] regions/page: %.1f" % (len(regions) / max(len(pages), 1)))

# %% [markdown]
# ## 5 · OCR — the GPU job
#
# `ocr.transcribe` groups regions **by page** and runs Nougat **once per page**,
# not once per region. That is not a shortcut: `facebook/nougat-base` was trained
# to read a whole page and emit `.mmd`, so per-page inference is both the faster
# path and the more accurate one (it keeps full-page context). The page transcript
# is then split back across that page's regions using Step 10's reading order.
#
# Three safeguards are already built into the reader (Step 11):
#
# 1. **Resumable** — a page whose `.mmd` exists is not re-inferred.
# 2. **Token cap** (`max_new_tokens=1536`) — well under Nougat's 4096 limit,
#    because a decoder running to the true limit on a dense table is precisely the
#    degeneration case, and paying for it on a page we will discard is waste.
# 3. **Degeneration detector** — a repeated-n-gram tail marks the page **failed**
#    and writes it to `data/ocr/failures.json` rather than writing garbage.
#
# We OCR the gated smoke subset first in **both** modes (free, thanks to
# resumability), sanity-check it, and only then let the full book run.

# %%
smoke_regions = [r for r in regions if r.page_id in smoke_ids]
print("OCR pass 1 (gated subset): %d regions across %d pages"
      % (len(smoke_regions), len({r.page_id for r in smoke_regions})))

t0 = time.time()
smoke_chunks = ocr_mod.transcribe(smoke_regions, cfg)
T_OCR_SMOKE = time.time() - t0
n_smoke_pages = len(glob.glob("data/ocr/*.mmd"))
print("\n[timing] gated subset: %.1f min (%d chunks, %d .mmd on disk)"
      % (T_OCR_SMOKE / 60, len(smoke_chunks), n_smoke_pages))

# %% [markdown]
# ## 6 · The sanity gate
#
# This is the checkpoint the whole two-phase protocol exists for. It fails loudly
# rather than letting a broken configuration quietly produce 1040 useless files.
#
# It checks four things that a genuinely-working reader must satisfy and a broken
# one will not:
#
# 1. **Transcripts exist and are non-trivial** — a page of A&S has hundreds of
#    characters; empty or 20-character output means the model is not really reading.
# 2. **Output looks like maths** — LaTeX/markdown markers (`\`, `$`, `{`, `=`)
#    appear. Plain prose with no notation means Nougat is not in its trained regime.
# 3. **Chunk ids are well-formed** — `chapter|page|region[|formula]`, the encoding
#    retrieval and citation depend on (`summary.md` §3f).
# 4. **Degeneration is not epidemic** — a few dense tables failing is expected and
#    gets reported honestly; most of the subset failing means something is wrong.

# %%
GATE_MIN_CHARS = 200
GATE_MAX_FAIL_FRACTION = 0.5

mmd_files = sorted(glob.glob("data/ocr/*.mmd"))
gate_pages = [f for f in mmd_files if os.path.basename(f)[:-4] in smoke_ids]

lengths = {}
for f in gate_pages:
    lengths[os.path.basename(f)[:-4]] = len(open(f, encoding="utf-8").read())

failures = []
if os.path.exists(ocr_mod.FAILURES_PATH):
    failures = json.load(open(ocr_mod.FAILURES_PATH, encoding="utf-8"))
failed_ids = {row["page_id"] for row in failures}

produced = [pid for pid in smoke_ids if pid in lengths]
substantial = [pid for pid in produced if lengths[pid] >= GATE_MIN_CHARS]

print("gated pages requested : %d" % len(smoke_ids))
print("transcripts produced  : %d" % len(produced))
print("marked degenerate     : %d  %s" % (len(failed_ids & smoke_ids), sorted(failed_ids & smoke_ids)))
print("length >= %d chars   : %d" % (GATE_MIN_CHARS, len(substantial)))
if lengths:
    vals = sorted(lengths.values())
    print("transcript chars      : min %d / median %d / max %d"
          % (vals[0], vals[len(vals) // 2], vals[-1]))

sample_id = "as_p0255" if "as_p0255" in lengths else (produced[0] if produced else None)
if sample_id:
    text = open("data/ocr/%s.mmd" % sample_id, encoding="utf-8").read()
    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
    print("SAMPLE TRANSCRIPT — %s (printed page %s)" % (sample_id, sample_id[4:].lstrip("0")))
    print("=" * 78)
    print(text[:1500])
    print("... [%d chars total]" % len(text))

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("SAMPLE CHUNK IDS (citation anchors)")
print("=" * 78)
for c in smoke_chunks[:10]:
    print("  %-45s  %3d chars" % (c.id, len(c.text)))
with_formula = [c for c in smoke_chunks if c.id.count("|") >= 3]
print("\nchunks carrying a formula id: %d of %d" % (len(with_formula), len(smoke_chunks)))
for c in with_formula[:5]:
    print("  %s" % c.id)

latex_markers = sum(1 for pid in produced
                    if any(m in open("data/ocr/%s.mmd" % pid, encoding="utf-8").read()
                           for m in ("\\", "$", "{", "=")))

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("GATE RESULTS")
print("=" * 78)
checks = [
    ("transcripts produced for most gated pages",
     len(produced) >= 0.8 * len(smoke_ids)),
    ("transcripts are substantial (>=%d chars)" % GATE_MIN_CHARS,
     len(substantial) >= 0.7 * max(len(produced), 1)),
    ("output contains LaTeX/markdown notation",
     latex_markers >= 0.7 * max(len(produced), 1)),
    ("chunk ids are well formed (chapter|page|region)",
     all(c.id.count("|") >= 2 for c in smoke_chunks) and len(smoke_chunks) > 0),
    ("degeneration is not epidemic (<%d%% of gated pages)" % int(GATE_MAX_FAIL_FRACTION * 100),
     len(failed_ids & smoke_ids) <= GATE_MAX_FAIL_FRACTION * len(smoke_ids)),
]
for label, ok in checks:
    print("  [%s] %s" % ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL", label))

GATE_PASSED = all(ok for _, ok in checks)
print("\nGATE: %s" % ("PASSED — safe to run the full book" if GATE_PASSED else "FAILED"))
if not GATE_PASSED:
    raise RuntimeError(
        "Sanity gate failed on the %d-page subset. Do NOT launch the full run — "
        "read the sample transcript above and fix the cause first." % len(smoke_ids)
    )

# %% [markdown]
# ## 7 · The full book
#
# Only reached with a green gate. In `"smoke"` mode this cell is a no-op, so the
# same notebook is safe to run either way.
#
# Expect roughly **1.5–3 hours** on a T4 for ~1040 pages. `ocr.transcribe` logs
# progress every 50 pages; the pages already done in the gated pass are skipped.

# %%
if RUN_MODE == "full":
    print("Starting full-book OCR over %d regions / %d pages."
          % (len(regions), len({r.page_id for r in regions})))
    print("Pages already transcribed are skipped. Progress logs every 50 pages.\n")
    t0 = time.time()
    chunks = ocr_mod.transcribe(regions, cfg)
    T_OCR_FULL = time.time() - t0
    print("\n[timing] full-book OCR: %.2f h" % (T_OCR_FULL / 3600))
else:
    chunks = smoke_chunks
    T_OCR_FULL = 0.0
    print("RUN_MODE='smoke' — full-book pass skipped.")
    print("Review the sample transcript above, then set RUN_MODE='full' and re-push.")

mmd_files = sorted(glob.glob("data/ocr/*.mmd"))
print("\ntotal transcripts on disk: %d" % len(mmd_files))
print("total chunks produced    : %d" % len(chunks))

# %% [markdown]
# ## 8 · Honest failure accounting
#
# `plan.md` Step 16 point 3 and form §5 both ask for this explicitly: **count the
# pages that failed and report them**, rather than quietly shipping a smaller
# corpus and implying full coverage. Nougat's repetition-degeneration on dense
# numeric tables is a known, documented weakness of the baseline model — it is
# exactly the kind of failure the Sprint-4 fine-tune is meant to reduce, so having
# the number here makes the before/after comparison meaningful.

# %%
failures = []
if os.path.exists(ocr_mod.FAILURES_PATH):
    failures = json.load(open(ocr_mod.FAILURES_PATH, encoding="utf-8"))

pages_attempted = len(pages)
pages_ok = len(mmd_files)
pages_failed = len(failures)

print("pages attempted this run : %d" % pages_attempted)
print("transcripts on disk      : %d" % pages_ok)
print("degenerate / failed      : %d" % pages_failed)
if pages_attempted:
    print("failure rate             : %.2f%%" % (100.0 * pages_failed / pages_attempted))

if failures:
    print("\nfailed pages:")
    for row in failures:
        print("  %s  reason=%s  at=%s"
              % (row.get("page_id"), row.get("reason"), row.get("detected_at")))
else:
    print("\nNo degenerate pages recorded.")

# Per-page coverage table -> ocr_coverage.csv
import csv

coverage_rows = []
by_id = {p.id: p for p in pages}
for f in mmd_files:
    pid = os.path.basename(f)[:-4]
    text = open(f, encoding="utf-8").read()
    coverage_rows.append({
        "page_id": pid,
        "doc_id": by_id[pid].doc_id if pid in by_id else "",
        "n_chars": len(text),
        "n_words": len(text.split()),
        "status": "failed" if pid in {r["page_id"] for r in failures} else "ok",
    })

TOTAL_WORDS_OUR_OCR = sum(r["n_words"] for r in coverage_rows)
TOTAL_CHARS_OUR_OCR = sum(r["n_chars"] for r in coverage_rows)
print("\nwords transcribed by OUR OCR : %d" % TOTAL_WORDS_OUR_OCR)
print("chars transcribed by OUR OCR : %d" % TOTAL_CHARS_OUR_OCR)
if RUN_MODE == "full":
    floor = 60000
    print("configs/task.yaml floor      : %d words" % floor)
    print("floor met                    : %s"
          % ("YES" if TOTAL_WORDS_OUR_OCR >= floor else "NO — investigate before Step 30"))
    print("(data/validate.py enforces this from OUR OCR, never the archive text layer)")

# %% [markdown]
# ## 9 · The BEFORE numbers — baseline quality on the 3 gold pages
#
# This is the deliverable that Sprint 4 is measured against.
#
# We report **two** metrics because either one alone is misleading
# (`summary.md` §4e):
#
# - **char-level F1** (`metrics.ocr_f1`) — longest-common-*subsequence* based, so
#   it is sensitive to reading order. Both sides are normalised first
#   (`normalize_latex`: Unicode NFC, `\tfrac`->`\frac`, `\left(`->`(`, spacing
#   macros dropped) so we score *reading accuracy*, not notation style.
# - **exact formula-match rate** (`metrics.exact_formula_match`) — the fraction of
#   the page's numbered formulas reproduced **exactly**, aligned by A&S formula id.
#
# Why both: char-F1 flatters mathematics badly. S3 measured this while building
# Step 12 — corrupting 5% of characters on the real p.255 gold still reads
# **0.955 char-F1** while breaking **every single formula** on the page. A number
# that high next to an exact-match of 0.000 is why reporting one metric alone
# would be dishonest.
#
# **On aggregation:** `exact_formula_match` returns `0.0` for a page with no
# numbered formulas — printed 243 is a pure numeric table, so it has none, and a
# `0.0` there means "nothing to measure", not "read it wrong". Averaging that in
# blindly would drag the score down for a reason unrelated to OCR quality, so we
# weight each page by its formula count and report both aggregates.

# %%
labels = {}
for line in open("grading_kit/labels.jsonl", encoding="utf-8"):
    line = line.strip()
    if line:
        row = json.loads(line)
        labels[row["page_id"]] = row["text"]

per_page = []
for printed in GOLD_PRINTED_PAGES:
    pid = "as_p%04d" % printed
    mmd = "data/ocr/%s.mmd" % pid
    if pid not in labels:
        print("SKIP %s — no gold label" % pid)
        continue
    if not os.path.exists(mmd):
        print("SKIP %s — no transcript produced" % pid)
        continue

    gold = labels[pid]
    pred = open(mmd, encoding="utf-8").read()
    gold_formulas = metrics.extract_formulas(gold)
    pred_formulas = metrics.extract_formulas(pred)

    per_page.append({
        "page_id": pid,
        "printed_page": printed,
        "char_f1": round(metrics.ocr_f1(pred, gold), 4),
        "exact_formula_match": round(metrics.exact_formula_match(pred, gold), 4),
        "n_gold_formulas": len(gold_formulas),
        "n_pred_formulas": len(pred_formulas),
        "gold_chars": len(gold),
        "pred_chars": len(pred),
        "degenerate": pid in {r["page_id"] for r in failures},
    })

print("=" * 92)
print("BASELINE (pretrained facebook/nougat-base, NOT fine-tuned) — the BEFORE number")
print("=" * 92)
print("%-10s %8s %10s %12s %10s %10s" %
      ("page", "printed", "char-F1", "exact-form", "gold-form", "pred-form"))
print("-" * 92)
for r in per_page:
    print("%-10s %8d %10.4f %12.4f %10d %10d" %
          (r["page_id"], r["printed_page"], r["char_f1"],
           r["exact_formula_match"], r["n_gold_formulas"], r["n_pred_formulas"]))
print("-" * 92)

BASELINE = {}
if per_page:
    n = len(per_page)
    mean_f1 = sum(r["char_f1"] for r in per_page) / n
    mean_efm_unweighted = sum(r["exact_formula_match"] for r in per_page) / n
    total_formulas = sum(r["n_gold_formulas"] for r in per_page)
    weighted_efm = (
        sum(r["exact_formula_match"] * r["n_gold_formulas"] for r in per_page) / total_formulas
        if total_formulas else 0.0
    )
    print("%-10s %8s %10.4f %12.4f %10d" %
          ("MEAN", "-", mean_f1, mean_efm_unweighted, total_formulas))
    print("%-10s %8s %10s %12.4f   <- use this one (weighted by formula count)" %
          ("WEIGHTED", "-", "-", weighted_efm))
    print("=" * 92)

    BASELINE = {
        "mean_char_f1": round(mean_f1, 4),
        "mean_exact_formula_match_unweighted": round(mean_efm_unweighted, 4),
        "weighted_exact_formula_match": round(weighted_efm, 4),
        "total_gold_formulas": total_formulas,
        "n_gold_pages": n,
    }

    print("\nsummary.md 4e expects the FINE-TUNED reader to land at")
    print("char-F1 0.88-0.93 and exact-match 0.55-0.75. This baseline is the")
    print("BEFORE column; Step 29 measures AFTER on the full 39-page test set.")
else:
    print("No gold pages transcribed yet — run at least the smoke pass.")

# %% [markdown]
# ## 10 · Package everything into one download
#
# Two clearly separated top-level folders inside the zip, so unpacking is
# unambiguous:
#
# ```
# mathscholar_step16_baseline_ocr.zip
# |
# +-- data/ocr/                  <- unzip at the REPO ROOT (gitignored; feeds Steps 17 & 30)
# |     +-- as_pNNNN.mmd  x ~1040
# |     +-- meta.jsonl           per-chunk ocr_confidence + bbox
# |     +-- failures.json        the honest degenerate-page list
# |
# +-- step16_reports/            <- evidence for the A2 form; keep locally
#       +-- baseline_metrics.json
#       +-- baseline_metrics.md  paste-ready table
#       +-- ocr_coverage.csv     per-page chars/words/status
#       +-- run_manifest.json    full reproducibility record
#       +-- README.md
# ```
#
# We ship **only text**, never images: `data/pages/` and `data/interim/` are ~1 GB
# each and are regenerated exactly by `bash scripts/get_data.sh`, so shipping them
# would cost a gigabyte of download to reproduce something a script already
# reproduces deterministically.

# %%
if os.path.isdir(STAGE_DIR):
    shutil.rmtree(STAGE_DIR)
ocr_out = os.path.join(STAGE_DIR, "data", "ocr")
rep_out = os.path.join(STAGE_DIR, "step16_reports")
os.makedirs(ocr_out, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(rep_out, exist_ok=True)

for f in mmd_files:
    shutil.copy2(f, ocr_out)
for name in ("meta.jsonl", "failures.json"):
    p = os.path.join("data/ocr", name)
    if os.path.exists(p):
        shutil.copy2(p, ocr_out)

RUN_MANIFEST = {
    "step": 16,
    "title": "baseline full-book OCR (pretrained facebook/nougat-base)",
    "owner": "S1 Anuron Maitro (2105037)",
    "run_mode": RUN_MODE,
    "generated_at_utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
    "repo": {"url": REPO_URL, "branch": REPO_BRANCH,
             "commit": REPO_COMMIT, "subject": REPO_SUBJECT},
    "versions": VERSIONS,
    "gpu": (torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if torch.cuda.is_available() else "none (CPU)"),
    "models": {
        "ocr": cfg["ocr"]["model"],
        "ocr_revision": getattr(ocr_mod, "NOUGAT_REVISION", None),
        "ocr_finetuned": False,
        "ocr_max_new_tokens": getattr(ocr_mod, "MAX_NEW_TOKENS", None),
        "layout": cfg["layout"]["model"],
        "layout_revision": getattr(layout, "TATR_REVISION", None),
    },
    "config_yaml": cfg,
    "counts": {
        "content_pages_in_corpus": len(all_pages),
        "pages_processed_this_run": len(pages),
        "regions_detected": len(regions),
        "region_kinds": kinds,
        "transcripts_on_disk": len(mmd_files),
        "chunks_produced": len(chunks),
        "pages_failed_degenerate": len(failures),
        "words_from_our_ocr": TOTAL_WORDS_OUR_OCR,
        "chars_from_our_ocr": TOTAL_CHARS_OUR_OCR,
    },
    "timings_seconds": {
        "corpus_render": round(T_RENDER, 1),
        "loader": round(T_LOAD, 1),
        "preprocess": round(T_PREPROCESS, 1),
        "layout": round(T_LAYOUT, 1),
        "ocr_gated_subset": round(T_OCR_SMOKE, 1),
        "ocr_full_book": round(T_OCR_FULL, 1),
        "total": round(time.time() - RUN_STARTED, 1),
    },
    "baseline_metrics": BASELINE,
    "baseline_per_page": per_page,
    "failures": failures,
}

with open(os.path.join(rep_out, "run_manifest.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    json.dump(RUN_MANIFEST, f, indent=2)

with open(os.path.join(rep_out, "baseline_metrics.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    json.dump({"run_mode": RUN_MODE, "aggregate": BASELINE, "per_page": per_page,
               "failures": failures}, f, indent=2)

with open(os.path.join(rep_out, "ocr_coverage.csv"), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
    w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["page_id", "doc_id", "n_chars", "n_words", "status"])
    w.writeheader()
    w.writerows(sorted(coverage_rows, key=lambda r: r["page_id"]))

md = []
md.append("# Step 16 — baseline OCR (BEFORE numbers)\n")
md.append("Reader: `%s` (**pretrained, not fine-tuned**), revision `%s`.\n"
          % (cfg["ocr"]["model"], getattr(ocr_mod, "NOUGAT_REVISION", "n/a")))
md.append("Run mode: `%s` · repo commit `%s` · GPU `%s`.\n"
          % (RUN_MODE, REPO_COMMIT[:12], RUN_MANIFEST["gpu"]))
md.append("\n## Per-page baseline on the 3 A1 gold pages\n")
md.append("| page | printed | char-F1 | exact-formula | gold formulas | pred formulas |")
md.append("|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|")
for r in per_page:
    md.append("| `%s` | %d | %.4f | %.4f | %d | %d |"
              % (r["page_id"], r["printed_page"], r["char_f1"],
                 r["exact_formula_match"], r["n_gold_formulas"], r["n_pred_formulas"]))
if BASELINE:

#    band `summary.md` §4e predicts for the fine-tuned model — that gap is the
#    thing Sprint 4 has to close. A baseline that is already at 0.95 would mean
#    something is wrong with the measurement, not that we are done.
# 4. If all three look right: set `RUN_MODE = "full"` and push again.
#

#
# 1. Download `mathscholar_step16_baseline_ocr.zip` from the notebook's **Output**
#    panel (or `kaggle kernels output`).
# 2. Unzip it at the repo root so `data/ocr/` is populated (gitignored).
# 3. Copy the numbers from `step16_reports/baseline_metrics.md` into
#    `notebooks/kb_demo.ipynb` (the scratch cell) and `CHANGELOG.md`, per
#    `plan.md` Step 16 point 5.
# 4. Commit, PR, merge, then hand Step 17 to S2.
#
# ### If the session timed out mid-run
#
# Nothing is lost. Add this run's **Output** as an **Input** to the next version
# and re-run — section 3 seeds `data/ocr/` from it and OCR resumes from where it
# stopped.
'''


def build(src: str) -> dict:
    cells = []
    kind = None
    buf: list[str] = []

    def flush() -> None:
        if kind is None:
            return
        text = "\n".join(buf).strip("\n")
        if not text.strip():
            return
        if kind == "markdown":
            cells.append({"cell_type": "markdown", "metadata": {},
                          "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)})
        else:
            cells.append({"cell_type": "code", "execution_count": None, "metadata": {},
                          "outputs": [], "source": text.splitlines(keepends=True)})

    for line in src.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("# %% [markdown]"):
            flush()
            kind, buf = "markdown", []
        elif line.startswith("# %%"):
            flush()
            kind, buf = "code", []
        elif kind == "markdown":
            buf.append(line[2:] if line.startswith("# ") else (line[1:] if line == "#" else line))
        elif kind == "code":
            buf.append(line)
    flush()

    return {
        "cells": cells,
        "metadata": {
            "kernelspec": {"display_name": "Python 3", "language": "python", "name": "python3"},
            "language_info": {"name": "python"},
        },
        "nbformat": 4,
        "nbformat_minor": 5,
    }


out = Path(sys.argv[1])
nb = build(SRC)
out.write_text(json.dumps(nb, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
n_md = sum(1 for c in nb["cells"] if c["cell_type"] == "markdown")
n_code = sum(1 for c in nb["cells"] if c["cell_type"] == "code")
print(f"wrote {out}  ({len(nb['cells'])} cells: {n_md} markdown, {n_code} code)")

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""MathScholar — drive the Kaggle Step 16 notebook from the terminal.

    python KAGGLE/push.py smoke     # set RUN_MODE="smoke", push + start the run
    python KAGGLE/push.py full      # set RUN_MODE="full",  push + start the run
    python KAGGLE/push.py status    # is it queued / running / complete / error?
    python KAGGLE/push.py log       # tail the running notebook's log
    python KAGGLE/push.py output    # download outputs into KAGGLE/output/

`kaggle kernels push` both saves AND starts a headless run (the API equivalent of
Save & Run All), so the job survives closing your laptop. GPU + internet + the
T4 x2 accelerator all come from kernel-metadata.json, so there is nothing to
click in the Kaggle UI.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
NOTEBOOK = HERE / "kaggle.ipynb"
METADATA = HERE / "kernel-metadata.json"
OUTPUT_DIR = HERE / "output"

KERNEL_ID = json.loads(METADATA.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["id"]
KERNEL_URL = f"https://www.kaggle.com/code/{KERNEL_ID.split('/', 1)[1]}"


def _run(args: list[str]) -> int:
    print("$", " ".join(args), flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(args).returncode


def current_mode() -> str | None:
    nb = json.loads(NOTEBOOK.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    for cell in nb["cells"]:
        for line in cell.get("source", []):
            m = re.match(r'^RUN_MODE\s*=\s*"(smoke|full)"', line)
            if m:
                return m.group(1)
    return None


def set_mode(mode: str) -> None:
    """Rewrite the single RUN_MODE assignment in the config cell."""
    nb = json.loads(NOTEBOOK.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    changed = False
    for cell in nb["cells"]:
        src = cell.get("source", [])
        for i, line in enumerate(src):
            if re.match(r'^RUN_MODE\s*=\s*"(smoke|full)"', line):
                src[i] = re.sub(
                    r'^RUN_MODE\s*=\s*"(smoke|full)"', f'RUN_MODE = "{mode}"', line
                )
                changed = True
    if not changed:
        sys.exit("ERROR: could not find the RUN_MODE assignment in the notebook.")
    NOTEBOOK.write_text(json.dumps(nb, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"RUN_MODE set to {mode!r}")


def push(mode: str) -> None:
    set_mode(mode)
    # 12 h is the Kaggle GPU ceiling; the smoke pass needs nothing like it, and a
    # tight timeout means a hung smoke run fails fast instead of idling for hours.
    timeout = "3600" if mode == "smoke" else "43200"
    rc = _run(["kaggle", "kernels", "push", "-p", str(HERE), "-t", timeout])
    if rc != 0:
        sys.exit(rc)
    print()
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"  pushed and RUNNING in mode: {mode}")
    print(f"  watch it:  {KERNEL_URL}")
    print("  poll:      python KAGGLE/push.py status")
    if mode == "smoke":
        print("\n  Expect ~15 min. Review the sample transcript, chunk ids and")
        print("  gold-page numbers BEFORE running:  python KAGGLE/push.py full")
    else:
        print("\n  Expect ~2-3 h. When it says complete:")
        print("     python KAGGLE/push.py output")
    print("=" * 70)


def main() -> None:
    cmd = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "status"
    if cmd in ("smoke", "full"):
        push(cmd)
    elif cmd == "status":
        print(f"notebook RUN_MODE in file: {current_mode()}")
        _run(["kaggle", "kernels", "status", KERNEL_ID])
    elif cmd == "log":
        _run(["kaggle", "kernels", "output", KERNEL_ID, "-p", str(OUTPUT_DIR)])
        log = OUTPUT_DIR / f"{KERNEL_ID.split('/', 1)[1]}.log"
        if log.exists():
            entries = json.loads(log.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            for e in entries[-60:]:
                print(e.get("data", "").rstrip())
        else:
            print("no log yet — the run may still be queued")
    elif cmd == "output":
        OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        rc = _run(["kaggle", "kernels", "output", KERNEL_ID, "-p", str(OUTPUT_DIR)])
        if rc == 0:
            print(f"\ndownloaded into: {OUTPUT_DIR}")
            for p in sorted(OUTPUT_DIR.rglob("*")):
                if p.is_file():
                    print(f"  {p.relative_to(OUTPUT_DIR)}  ({p.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)")
    else:
        sys.exit(__doc__)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

That last one produced a genuinely useful result. Feeding the gold text in as its own prediction (a perfect reader):

aggregation	score
unweighted exact-formula-match	0.667
weighted by formula count	1.000
A flawless transcription scores 0.667 unweighted, purely because p.243 is a numeric table with 0 formulas contributing a 0.0. That's Elias's warning demonstrated concretely rather than taken on faith — the notebook reports both numbers and labels the weighted one as the one to use.

Design decisions worth flagging
Rendering the whole book even in smoke mode. LIMIT=20 in get_data.sh would render the first 20 PDF pages — all front matter, which loader.py drops — giving zero content pages. Smoke subsets the Page list after loading instead, which also skips preprocess+layout on ~1020 pages.
Not installing requirements.lock on Kaggle. It pins torch==2.3.1, which would fight Kaggle's CUDA torch and could silently land you on a CPU wheel. Only pymupdf + transformers==4.44.2 (matching the lock) get installed.
Even full mode OCRs the 20 gated pages first and hard-fails on a bad gate before touching the book — free, because transcribe skips existing .mmd.
One sequencing point you need to know
Step 16's repo deliverables are the numbers, and those don't exist until the full run finishes. So this is genuinely two commits at two different times:

Now-ish — the Kaggle notebook is outside the repo, so there may be nothing to commit until the run produces data.
After the full run — the BEFORE numbers go into notebooks/kb_demo.ipynb (plan.md Step 16 point 5 says exactly this) and CHANGELOG.md (yours to edit).
I won't fabricate numbers into those files. I'll fill them from the real output once the full run lands, then give you the complete git sequence.

I'll report back with an honest read on the transcript quality, chunk ids, and baseline numbers as soon as the smoke run finishes.

 614          Returns:
 615              Union[str, List[str]]: The postprocessed text or list of postprocessed texts.
 616          """
 617          requires_backends(self, ["nltk", "levenshtein"])
 618  
 619          if isinstance(generation, list):
 620              if num_workers is not None and isinstance(num_workers, int):

 622                      return p.map(partial(self.post_process_single, fix_markdown=fix_markdown), generation)
 623              else:
 624                  return [self.post_process_single(s, fix_markdown=fix_markdown) for s in generation]
 625          else:
 626              return self.post_process_single(generation, fix_markdown=fix_markdown)

Confirmed the root cause precisely. Here's what those warnings mean.

The warning: ocr_confidence is silently fake
vision/ocr.py computes per-page confidence via:


scores = self._model.compute_transition_scores(
    outputs.sequences, outputs.scores, normalize_logits=True)
Inside transformers, normalize_logits=True runs scores.reshape(-1, self.config.vocab_size, ...) (utils.py:1115). But the model is a VisionEncoderDecoderModel, and I just verified against the real config:


has top-level vocab_size? False
c.vocab_size RAISES: AttributeError 'VisionEncoderDecoderConfig' object has no attribute 'vocab_size'
c.decoder.vocab_size: 50000
The vocab size lives on config.decoder, not the top level. So it raises AttributeError on every page, the bare except Exception swallows it, and confidence stays at its hardcoded fallback.

Consequence: every row in data/ocr/meta.jsonl will read "ocr_conf": 0.5 — a constant masquerading as a measurement. summary.md §3f specifies that sidecar as real per-chunk confidence, and it feeds the "Calibrated" NFR in A3.

What it does NOT affect: the OCR text itself, or Step 16's BEFORE numbers. The exception fires after decoding and post-processing. char-F1 and exact-formula-match are untouched. So this run's headline deliverable is still valid.

Two secondary defects it exposes: the except Exception logs no exception text (I had to reverse-engineer it from source), and a fallback that silently substitutes a plausible-looking number is worse than one that records "unavailable".

The bigger thing those timestamps reveal — speed
The warnings are one per page, so they're a clean stopwatch:


1525.6 → 1545.9 → 1566.1 → 1586.5 → 1606.7 → 1626.8 → 1646.9 → 1666.8 → 1687.2
deltas:  20.3   20.2   20.4   20.2   20.1   20.1   19.9   20.4     ≈ 19.8 s/page
Extrapolated to the full book: 1040 × ~19.8 s ≈ 5.7 h of OCR, plus ~20 min render, ~5 min preprocess, ~30 min layout → ≈ 6.5 h total, not the 2–3 h plan.md estimated.

Caveat in your favour: my 20 smoke pages deliberately over-sample dense tables (the hard, token-heavy case), so the book average is probably lower — call it 4–6.5 h.

That still fits inside Kaggle's 12 h batch limit, but it's ~6 GPU-hr of your ~30/week, and Steps 28 and 30 both need GPU too (~5 h and ~6 h). Projected total ≈ 18 GPU-hr, which leaves little room for a retry.

Likely cause: Reader._ensure_loaded() never sets torch_dtype, so Nougat runs in fp32 on a T4. fp16 is what Nougat's own implementation uses and typically gives 2–3× on T4 — potentially 20 s → ~7 s/page, turning 6.5 h into ~2.5 h.

Both the confidence bug and the fp32 issue live in src/doc_agent/vision/ocr.py — Himadri's Step 11 file, and neither blocks Step 16 (unlike the missing deps, which did). So I haven't touched it. That's a call for you, and I'll ask once the smoke results are in and you can see actual transcript quality alongside it.

Poller is still running; the run is ~28 min in and should land shortly. I'll report the transcripts, chunk ids and baseline numbers as soon as it does.

The low char-F1 is real. Nougat was trained on modern single-column arXiv LaTeX; A&S is a 1964 two-column scan that's ~half dense numeric tables. It's emitting only 15–34% of each page. That's a legitimate BEFORE number with big headroom — good for the fine-tuning story.

But three instrumentation bugs make the reported numbers wrong
1. exact_formula_match = 0.0000 is structurally impossible to beat. Nougat writes **6.1.1**: \(\Gamma(z)...\); extract_formulas requires 6.1.1   at line start. It parsed 0 formulas from output that demonstrably contains 6.1.1, 6.1.2, 6.1.3. So that metric currently measures format agreement, not correctness. (Elias's eval/metrics.py)

2. We under-report failures by 4×. Nougat emits its own [MISSING_PAGE_POST] marker — we ignore it entirely:

We reported 1/20 (5%). True rate is ≥4/20 (20%), arguably 30% counting near-empty pages. _is_degenerate only inspects the tail, so p.255's mid-page \! flood slipped through. Form §5 explicitly asks for an honest failure count — this one isn't. (Himadri's vision/ocr.py)

3. ocr_conf is a constant. Confirmed: 201 chunk rows, distinct values {0.5} — the config.vocab_size AttributeError I diagnosed. (Himadri's vision/ocr.py)

I'll also own a mistake: my sanity gate passed this. It checked plumbing (does it emit LaTeX-ish text of reasonable length) not quality (does it resemble gold). It should have compared against the gold pages, which were right there. I'll fix that.

import glob, os, re
# a 1-4 char unit repeated 30+ times in a row
PAT = re.compile(r"(.{1,4}?)\1{29,}", re.DOTALL)
print("longest consecutive short-substring repeat per transcript:")
for f in sorted(glob.glob("KAGGLE/output/ocr_live/*.mmd")):
    s=open(f,encoding="utf-8").read()
    m=PAT.search(s)
    pid=os.path.basename(f)[:-4]
    if m:
        unit=m.group(1); reps=len(m.group(0))//max(len(unit),1)
        print(f"  {pid:<11} MATCH  unit={unit!r} x{reps}")
    else:
        # report the best sub-threshold run so we can see the margin
        best=0; bestu=None
        for k in (1,2,3,4):
            for i in range(0,len(s)-k,1):
                u=s[i:i+k]; n=1
                while s[i+n*k:i+(n+1)*k]==u: n+=1
                if n>best: best,bestu=n,u
        print(f"  {pid:<11} clean  (max run: {bestu!r} x{best})")

# ## 6 · The sanity gate
#
# This is the checkpoint the whole two-phase protocol exists for. It fails loudly
# rather than letting a broken configuration quietly produce 1040 useless files.
#
# It checks four things that a genuinely-working reader must satisfy and a broken
# one will not:
#
# 1. **Transcripts exist and are non-trivial** — a page of A&S has hundreds of
#    characters; empty or 20-character output means the model is not really reading.
# 2. **Output looks like maths** — LaTeX/markdown markers (`\`, `$`, `{`, `=`)
#    appear. Plain prose with no notation means Nougat is not in its trained regime.
# 3. **Chunk ids are well-formed** — `chapter|page|region[|formula]`, the encoding
#    retrieval and citation depend on (`summary.md` §3f).
# 4. **Degeneration is not epidemic** — a few dense tables failing is expected and
#    gets reported honestly; most of the subset failing means something is wrong.

# %%

GATE_MIN_CHARS = 200
GATE_MAX_FAIL_FRACTION = 0.5

mmd_files = sorted(glob.glob("data/ocr/*.mmd"))
gate_pages = [f for f in mmd_files if os.path.basename(f)[:-4] in smoke_ids]

lengths = {}
for f in gate_pages:
    lengths[os.path.basename(f)[:-4]] = len(open(f, encoding="utf-8").read())

failures = []
if os.path.exists(ocr_mod.FAILURES_PATH):
    failures = json.load(open(ocr_mod.FAILURES_PATH, encoding="utf-8"))
failed_ids = {row["page_id"] for row in failures}

produced = [pid for pid in smoke_ids if pid in lengths]
substantial = [pid for pid in produced if lengths[pid] >= GATE_MIN_CHARS]

print("gated pages requested : %d" % len(smoke_ids))
print("transcripts produced  : %d" % len(produced))
print("marked degenerate     : %d  %s" % (len(failed_ids & smoke_ids), sorted(failed_ids & smoke_ids)))
print("length >= %d chars   : %d" % (GATE_MIN_CHARS, len(substantial)))
if lengths:
    vals = sorted(lengths.values())
    print("transcript chars      : min %d / median %d / max %d"
          % (vals[0], vals[len(vals) // 2], vals[-1]))

sample_id = "as_p0255" if "as_p0255" in lengths else (produced[0] if produced else None)
if sample_id:
    text = open("data/ocr/%s.mmd" % sample_id, encoding="utf-8").read()
    print("\n" + "=" * 78)
    print("SAMPLE TRANSCRIPT — %s (printed page %s)" % (sample_id, sample_id[4:].lstrip("0")))
    print("=" * 78)
    print(text[:1500])
    print("... [%d chars total]" % len(text))

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("SAMPLE CHUNK IDS (citation anchors)")
print("=" * 78)
for c in smoke_chunks[:10]:
    print("  %-45s  %3d chars" % (c.id, len(c.text)))
with_formula = [c for c in smoke_chunks if c.id.count("|") >= 3]
print("\nchunks carrying a formula id: %d of %d" % (len(with_formula), len(smoke_chunks)))
for c in with_formula[:5]:
    print("  %s" % c.id)

latex_markers = sum(1 for pid in produced
                    if any(m in open("data/ocr/%s.mmd" % pid, encoding="utf-8").read()
                           for m in ("\\", "$", "{", "=")))

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("GATE RESULTS")
print("=" * 78)
checks = [
    ("transcripts produced for most gated pages",
     len(produced) >= 0.8 * len(smoke_ids)),
    ("transcripts are substantial (>=%d chars)" % GATE_MIN_CHARS,
     len(substantial) >= 0.7 * max(len(produced), 1)),
    ("output contains LaTeX/markdown notation",
     latex_markers >= 0.7 * max(len(produced), 1)),
    ("chunk ids are well formed (chapter|page|region)",
     all(c.id.count("|") >= 2 for c in smoke_chunks) and len(smoke_chunks) > 0),
    ("degeneration is not epidemic (<%d%% of gated pages)" % int(GATE_MAX_FAIL_FRACTION * 100),
     len(failed_ids & smoke_ids) <= GATE_MAX_FAIL_FRACTION * len(smoke_ids)),
]
for label, ok in checks:
    print("  [%s] %s" % ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL", label))

GATE_PASSED = all(ok for _, ok in checks)
print("\nGATE: %s" % ("PASSED — safe to run the full book" if GATE_PASSED else "FAILED"))
if not GATE_PASSED:
    raise RuntimeError(
        "Sanity gate failed on the %d-page subset. Do NOT launch the full run — "
        "read the sample transcript above and fix the cause first." % len(smoke_ids)
    )

# book** over that is worse than no gate, because it converts "unverified" into
# "verified" without doing any verifying.

# The gold pages were sitting right there, unused. So now the gate reads them.
#
# ### What it checks now
#
# **Hard checks — these raise and abort the run:**
#
# 1. Every gold page produced a transcript at all.
# 2. Chunk ids are well formed (`chapter|page|region[|formula]`).
# 3. `extract_formulas` parses a non-zero number of formulas *from the reader's own
#    output* on at least one gold page. Zero across the board is the signature of a
#    parser/format mismatch rather than a bad reader — the exact bug that made run
#    #2's exact-match meaningless.
# 4. **fp16 regression check.** Run #2's fp32 char-F1 is recorded below. If half
#    precision has degraded quality beyond tolerance, that is a real finding and the
#    run stops rather than spending 2+ h producing a worse corpus.
#
# **Reported loudly, but not gating** — because these are *measurements*, and a gate
# that fails on a low baseline would be a gate that refuses to let us measure a bad

    by_reason[row["reason"]] = by_reason.get(row["reason"], 0) + 1

print(f"pages attempted      : {N_CONTENT_PAGES}")
print(f"transcripts produced : {len(mmd_files)}")
print(f"failed / degenerate  : {len(failures)}  ({100 * len(failures) / N_CONTENT_PAGES:.1f}%)")
for reason, count in sorted(by_reason.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
    print(f"   {reason:<28} {count:>4}  ({100 * count / len(failures):.1f}% of failures)")

words = sum(len(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").split()) for p in mmd_files)
print(f"\\nwords from OUR OCR   : {words}  (task.yaml floor: 60,000 -- {'MET' if words >= 60000 else 'NOT MET'})")

gold: dict[str, str] = {}
for line in LABELS_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    line = line.strip()
    if line:
        row = json.loads(line)
        gold[row["page_id"]] = row["text"]

print(f"\\n{\'page\':<10} {\'char-F1\':>9} {\'exact-form\':>12} {\'gold-form\':>10} {\'pred-form\':>10}  status")
print("-" * 72)
failed_reason = {row["page_id"]: row["reason"] for row in failures}
scored = []
for pid in ("as_p0243", "as_p0255", "as_p0360"):
    mmd = OCR_DIR / f"{pid}.mmd"
    if not mmd.exists():
        reason = failed_reason.get(pid, "?")
        print(f"{pid:<10} {\'--\':>9} {\'--\':>12} {\'--\':>10} {\'--\':>10}  FAILED: {reason}")
        continue
    pred = mmd.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    g = gold[pid]
    f1 = metrics.ocr_f1(pred, g)
    ex = metrics.exact_formula_match(pred, g)
    ngf = len(metrics.extract_formulas(g))
    npf = len(metrics.extract_formulas(pred))
    print(f"{pid:<10} {f1:>9.4f} {ex:>12.4f} {ngf:>10} {npf:>10}  ok")
    scored.append((pid, f1, ex, ngf))
print("-" * 72)

if scored:
    mean_f1 = sum(s[1] for s in scored) / len(scored)
    total_f = sum(s[3] for s in scored)
    weighted_ex = (
        sum(s[2] * s[3] for s in scored) / total_f if total_f else 0.0
    )
    print(f"mean char-F1 (n={len(scored)} gold page(s) with a transcript): {mean_f1:.4f}")
    print(f"exact-formula-match, weighted by formula count: {weighted_ex:.4f}")

print("\\nsummary.md 4e expects the FINE-TUNED reader to land at char-F1 0.88-0.93,")
print("exact-match 0.55-0.75. This is the pretrained BEFORE number Step 29 compares against.")

### Step 16 notes (baseline OCR — the real BEFORE number, and 3 blocking fixes)
- **Full-book baseline run on Kaggle T4×2**: pretrained `facebook/nougat-base` (NOT fine-tuned —
  fine-tuning is Step 28) over all 1040 content pages. 594 succeeded, **446 failed (42.9%)**:
  70.4% empty-or-near-empty, 18.4% Nougat's own `[MISSING_PAGE]` marker, 11.2% repetition-
  degeneration. Failures span 28/29 chapters but skew hard toward table-dense ones —
  `ch04_elem_transcend` lost 61% of its pages vs. 43% book-wide, matching summary.md §4e's own
  prediction that tables would be the weak point. Words from our OCR: 87,523 (floor: 60,000, met).
- **The BEFORE number**: only 1 of the 3 permanent gold pages (as_p0360) produced a transcript —
  char-F1 **0.4166**. as_p0243 and as_p0255 fail deterministically (documented reasons), which is
  real evidence for Step 29's before/after story, not a measurement gap.
- **Found and fixed 3 bugs surfaced by this run, all now on this branch**:
  1. `nltk` + `python-Levenshtein` were declared nowhere in `pyproject.toml`/lockfiles, so
     `vision/ocr.py`'s call to `post_process_generation()` raised `ImportError` on *any* clean
     install, not just Kaggle — reproduced locally to confirm. Added both deps, regenerated locks.
  2. `ocr_confidence` was silently pinned at a constant 0.5 for every chunk: `compute_transition_
     scores(..., normalize_logits=True)` reshapes by `self.config.vocab_size`, which
     `VisionEncoderDecoderConfig` doesn't define (it's on `config.decoder`). Replaced with a
     direct log-softmax readout.
  3. The repetition-degeneration detector only checked the tail, missing mid-page spirals
     (measured undercounting the true failure rate by ~4x on a 20-page sample: 5% reported vs.
     35% actual). Added a whole-page repeated-unit check plus Nougat's own `[MISSING_PAGE]`
     marker and a near-empty-output floor.
- **fp16 on GPU** (fp32 stays on CPU): real but modest speedup, 14.7s/page vs 17.4s/page fp32
  (~15%, not the hoped-for 2-3x). No measurable quality regression on the one page comparable
  across both precisions (+0.0036 char-F1).
- `KAGGLE/` (notebook, push helper, kernel metadata) lives outside the repo per the "no notebook
  named in the spec" rule — reproducible via `python KAGGLE/push.py full`.
That's the earlier (slower) download attempt finally finishing — it's superseded; I already pulled the same data via a fresh download, verified it byte-for-byte against the run log, and finished the Step 16 work (populated data/ocr/, built and executed the kb_demo.ipynb scratch cell, ran all CI gates green). Nothing new here — quick sanity check to be sure, then no further action needed.

Now the two substantive questions.

1. How do the 446 failed pages get fixed?
Honestly: partially, and that's by design, not a gap.

The mechanism is Step 30 — re-OCR the whole book with the fine-tuned reader (plan.md Step 30, owned by S3/Elias). Fine-tuning (Sprint 4) trains specifically on A&S-style degraded scans + real A&S table/formula pages, which should substantially reduce the two dominant failure modes here (empty-output, repetition-degeneration) since both stem from the pretrained model being out-of-distribution on our specific scan style.

But summary.md §4e — written before any of this was measured — already predicted the honest limit: "tables worst... because dense grids are a structural problem fine-tuning doesn't fix." The chapter breakdown I found (ch04_elem_transcend at 61% failure, almost entirely dense numeric tables) is exactly that predicted weak point, now measured instead of assumed. Some of these pages will likely still fail after fine-tuning — LoRA adapts glyph/notation style, not the decoder's fundamental tendency to degenerate on structurally unfamiliar content.

This isn't a problem to solve before Sprint 4 — it's what Sprint 4 is for, and plan.md Step 30 already expects to report "pages indexed / 1046" as a real, possibly-incomplete number (not silently assumed to be 100%). If the residual rate after fine-tuning is still too high, there are levers to consider then (raising MAX_NEW_TOKENS for likely-table pages, falling back to transcribe_region() per-region on chronic failures) — but that's a Sprint-4-time decision with real data in hand, not something to guess at now.

2. data/ocr/ and the gitignore — you're right to push on this, and I found something concrete
I measured rather than assumed:

It doesn't actually describe data/ocr/, which is plain text and is nowhere near that size, even at full book coverage.

More importantly, your own .gitignore already has the precedent for exactly this situation:


# ...but the LoRA adapter IS a submitted artifact (needed to reproduce our numbers),

data/ocr/ fits that same justification — a grader or teammate re-executing kb_demo.ipynb from a clean clone needs it to reproduce the 0.4166 char-F1 number; without it, the cell throws FileNotFoundError. And it isn't "the corpus" that summary.md says never to commit (that's the source page images — data/raw/, data/pages/, data/interim/, which correctly stay ignored) — it's our own derived work product, same category as the LoRA adapter.

This also solves your practical concern directly: Himadri needs draft OCR for Step 17's annotation helper. If data/ocr/ is committed, he gets it from git pull — no 5-hour Kaggle run on his own account.

I haven't touched .gitignore or plan.md's §11.6 table yet — that table currently says OCR output should stay ❌ gitignored, and both files are shared team conventions that affect how Steps 17/29/30 work, so this isn't mine to change unilaterally.

Confirmed. The kernel's display name is generic ("Python 3 (ipykernel)"), so in a picker with multiple Python installs it's easy to grab the wrong one by name alone — what matters is the interpreter path, not the label.

What happened
I ran kb_demo.ipynb via nbclient, invoked from a shell where doc-agent-1/.venv was activated. Installing ipykernel into that venv earlier (for this exact purpose) auto-registered it as the python3 kernel — and it's the only Jupyter kernel on this machine right now, pointing at doc-agent-1/.venv/Scripts/python.exe, which has pydantic, torch, transformers, and everything else the project pins in pyproject.toml.

Your run hit ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pydantic' because VS Code's notebook UI had a different Python kernel selected — some other interpreter (system Python, a different venv, Anaconda, whatever VS Code defaulted to) that never had this project's dependencies installed. sys.path.insert(0, "../src") only tells that kernel where to find the doc_agent package — it can't make pydantic exist inside an environment that never installed it. This isn't a bug in the notebook or in metrics.py/contracts.py; it's a kernel-selection mismatch, and it's exactly why a "genuine fresh execution" claim needs the right interpreter to mean anything.

Fix — select the correct kernel in VS Code
Open kb_demo.ipynb.
Top-right of the notebook, click the kernel picker (shows something like "Select Kernel" or whatever's currently selected).
Choose "Select Another Kernel" → "Python Environments...".
Look for the entry whose path ends in doc-agent-1\.venv\Scripts\python.exe — not by the "Python 3 (ipykernel)" label, since that's generic and could match multiple environments. If VS Code doesn't list it automatically, choose "Enter interpreter path..." and paste that path directly.
Run the cells again.
One reassurance: this doesn't affect the grounding-gate evidence itself. The notebook file already has my real, correctly-executed output saved inside its JSON (that's what nbformat.write persisted) — a grader opening the file sees those results regardless of what kernel you happen to have selected locally. This only matters for you re-running it live to double-check, which is exactly the right thing to want to do — just point it at the right interpreter first.

Bash Sweep the repeat threshold on real data to find the right cutoff
IN
cd "f:/4-1/CSE 429/Project A1/doc-agent-1" && source .venv/Scripts/activate 2>/dev/null
python - <<'PY'
import re
from pathlib import Path

TABULAR_UNIT_RE = re.compile(r"^[lcr|@{}\s.0-9]*$")
WS = re.compile(r"\s+")
MIN_PAGE_CHARS = 120

known_genuine = ["as_p0778","as_p0405","as_p0934","as_p0289","as_p0752","as_p0950","as_p0837","as_p0878","as_p0049","as_p0177","as_p0360"]
files = sorted(Path("data/ocr").glob("*.mmd"))

def scan(unit_max, min_repeats):
    pat = re.compile(rf"(.{{1,{unit_max}}}?)\1{{{min_repeats-1},}}", re.DOTALL)
    flagged = []
    for f in files:
        t = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        if len(t.strip()) < MIN_PAGE_CHARS:
            continue
        stripped = WS.sub("", t)
        for m in pat.finditer(stripped):
            if not TABULAR_UNIT_RE.match(m.group(1)):
                flagged.append(f.stem)
                break
    return set(flagged)

for min_repeats in (20, 15, 13, 12, 10, 8):
    flagged = scan(20, min_repeats)
    caught = sum(1 for p in known_genuine if p in flagged)
    print(f"min_repeats={min_repeats:3d}: {len(flagged):3d} pages flagged total | {caught}/11 known-genuine caught | missed: {[p for p in known_genuine if p not in flagged]}")
PY

min_repeats= 15:  43 pages flagged total | 10/11 known-genuine caught | missed: ['as_p0289']
min_repeats= 13:  51 pages flagged total | 11/11 known-genuine caught | missed: []
min_repeats= 12:  52 pages flagged total | 11/11 known-genuine caught | missed: []

min_repeats=  8:  69 pages flagged total | 11/11 known-genuine caught | missed: []

from doc_agent.vision.ocr import DEGEN_REPEAT_RE, TABULAR_UNIT_RE, WS_RE, MIN_SPIRAL_SPAN_CHARS
from pathlib import Path

rows = []
for f in sorted(Path("data/ocr").glob("*.mmd")):
    text = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    stripped = text.strip()
    if len(stripped) < 120:
        continue
    no_ws = WS_RE.sub("", stripped)
    for m in DEGEN_REPEAT_RE.finditer(no_ws):
        span = m.end() - m.start()
        if span >= MIN_SPIRAL_SPAN_CHARS and not TABULAR_UNIT_RE.match(m.group(1)):
            rows.append((f.stem, m.group(1), span, len(no_ws)))
            break

rows.sort(key=lambda r: r[2]/r[3])
for pid, unit, span, total in rows[:15]:
    print(f"{pid}: unit={unit!r} span={span}/{total} ({100*span/total:.0f}%)")
